newsitem.title: FINLAND: Borealis Q1 pretax profit surges to FIM 326 mln.
newsitem.headline: Borealis Q1 pretax profit surges to FIM 326 mln.

text.p: Petrochemicals group Borealis -- owned by Finnish Neste and Norway's Statoil -- posted a 326 million markka pretax profit in the first quarter, up from 62 million in the year-ago period, Neste said on Monday.
Borealis' first quarter net sales totalled 3.3 billion markka versus 3.0 billion, and the operating profit rose to 343 million markka from 42 million, Neste said in a statement.

In a separate statement, Borealis said the year-on-year improvement was mainly due to "stronger markets and considerably better margins" which followed a strong rise in prices, and higher sales volumes in polyolefins.
"However, the gain from rising prices was reduced by a 35 percent increase in feed materials," it said.
Borealis said its first quarter operating cashflow was 319 million markka, up from 119 million a year earlier, and return on investment was 12 percent, up from five percent.
"Polyolefin prices are expected to continue to rise, while input materials prices are expected to remain stable and to settle at a lower level than in the first quarter," Borealis said.
